chunks: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
Whoever passes by orchards, there is no harm in eating from their fruits, but he should not carry anything from them away with him.

key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.بِبَسَاتِينِ: by orchards or gardens containing fruit trees
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.يَحْمِلْ: to carry away or take with oneself

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fruit when passing by someone else's orchard in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning passing by orchards and eating some of their fruit. It permits incidental eating on the spot while forbidding taking any of the fruit away, indicating a limit that preserves the rights of others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3678 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"Whoever passes by orchards, there is no harm in eating from their fruits, but he should not carry anything from them with him."
